# Corpus audio effect: signal behavior and reference renders

## Scope

Feature FEAT-DEVICES, T1 device audio ([ADR 0004](../decisions/adr-0004-target-scope-t1.md)).
User task: a track holds the bundled Corpus effect, and the offline render of that track
must sound as Live's would. This draft specifies:

- the output Corpus produces for a stereo input and a set of stored parameter values, at
  44.1 kHz and 48 kHz;
- the reference renders that define that output for T1, and the protocol that made them;
- the comparison metric a candidate render must meet.

How the parameters are stored, with their domains and defaults, is
[SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-PARAMETERS](bundled-device-parameters.md). Where Corpus sits in the
track's signal flow belongs to the mix-graph and playback specs.

Excluded:

- the MIDI side-chain features: MidiPitch, MidiGate, Transpose, FineTranspose,
  PitchBendRange, DecayOnNoteOff, MidiMode and the side-chain routing fields (REQ-013, U);
- LFO Sync and the random LFO shapes as exact waveforms (REQ-011);
- parameter automation during a render beyond the timing rules of REQ-012;
- display text, CPU load and latency reporting.

Every requirement is a **proposed contract**. Nothing was run against Live, and under
[ADR 0003](../decisions/adr-0003-no-reference-execution.md) nothing will be. The audio
evidence is extracted execution of the shipped x86_64 Corpus code. The Live-side
parameter path is a static derivation. Canonical evidence:
[device DSP by extracted execution](../research/device-dsp-extracted.md).

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-001 — reference renders define the output

- **X.** For T1, Corpus's output for an input and a set of host values is the reference render
  made with this protocol:
  1. a new instance is created;
  2. the sample rate is set (44,100 or 48,000 Hz);
  3. all 38 host values of REQ-002 are sent, in index order;
  4. processing starts at the first frame, in host blocks of 512 frames;
  5. the input is stereo binary32, flagged as present;
  6. the transport is not playing (position 0, 120 BPM).

  The reference renders are retained with their inputs and SHA-256 (cases below). The
  output is stereo binary32, one output frame for each input frame.
- **X.** With constant parameters the output does not depend on these choices:
  - the host block size (64, 256, 333, 512 and 2,048 frames tested);
  - flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero;
  - the clock value with which the device seeds its random generator, except for the random
    LFO shapes (REQ-011).

  Re-running a case gives a bit-identical render.
- **S, X.** Live creates the instance, sets the current sample rate and sends the parameter values
  ([N5](../research/device-parameter-mapping-native.md#how-live-loads-a-bundle)). It may also run
  a reset sequence: 1,024 frames of silent input, a device reset, then the ResonanceType value
  again. That sequence leaves the output of a later input unchanged within 4.6 × 10⁻²⁰ (X, default
  and Tube settings).
- **U.** When Live runs the reset sequence, which host block sizes it uses, and which
  transport and input-flag values it passes. Effect on T1: none for constant parameters
  (block-size invariance, X). The timing of parameter changes under REQ-012 depends on Live's
  block boundaries.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-002 — from stored values to host values

- **S** ([N5](../research/device-parameter-mapping-native.md#corpus-complete-38-indices)). Live
  sends 38 host values. Index i corresponds to the stored parameter in the order of the N5 table
  (0 ResonanceType … 37 MidiMode). Each stored value is first clamped to its domain
  (SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-PARAMETERS). Then:
  - **Enumerations and Booleans** pass as the index or as 0/1. These are ResonanceType,
    ResonatorQuality, LfoType, LfoSync, LfoStereoMode, FilterOn, LfoOnOff, MidiPitch, MidiGate and
    MidiMode.
  - **FilterMidFreq** in Hz passes as log₁₀(f/50)/log₁₀(360). 1000 Hz gives binary32 0.5089499354362488.
  - **DecayOnNoteOff** passes as 1 − v.
  - **Transpose, FineTranspose, PitchBendRange and LfoSyncRate** pass as the stored value rounded
    to the nearest 1/32768, then truncated toward zero.
  - **All others** pass unchanged.
- **X.** MidiMode (index 37) has no effect on the output (bit-identical with 1 and 0).
- **S-cond (A1).** ExcitationX, ListeningXL and ListeningXR pass unchanged.
- **U.** Whether A1 holds. Effect on T1: renders are defined for host position values. A stored
  position other than the default can be tied to a render only under A1. Without A1, sets that
  change these three parameters from their defaults are not verifiable.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-003 — controller values

The device turns each host value v into a controller value c between 0 and 127 (X; the
formulas are confirmed by the agreement of REQ-004 to 010):

| Rule | Host values | c |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U | 0..1 (values above 1 act as 1) | 128v if v ≤ 0.5, else 126v + 1 |
| B | −1..1 | 63.5v + 63.5 if v < 0, else 63v + 64 |
| P | positions | 64 + 31.5v |
| I | Radius | 127(1 − v) if 1 − v ≤ 0.5, else 126(1 − v) + 1 |

- **X.** The resonator controls take ⌊c⌋, so each has 128 steps. These controls are Decay,
  FreqDamping, Inharmonics, Ratio, Radius, AmpFreq, ExcitationX, ListeningXL, ListeningXR,
  TubeOpening and Bleed. Two host values with the same ⌊c⌋ give the same output: Decay 0.503
  renders bit-identically to Decay 0.5. The other controls use c unrounded.
- **Definitions (X).** Curves used below, with n = 0.5 when c = 64 and n = c/127 otherwise:
  - lin(c; lo, hi) = lo + n·(hi − lo);
  - exp(c; lo, hi) = lo·(hi/lo)^(c/127), which has no midpoint case.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-004 — dry and wet mix, drive, width and level

- **X.** DryWet: with a = U(DryWet)/127, the dry gain is P(0.25 − a/4) and the wet gain P(a/4).
  Here P(t) = t·(10.392633 − 31.177902t + 20.785267t²). DryWet 0 passes the input at
  0.974309 (−0.226 dB). DryWet 1 removes the dry signal.
- **X.** Drive multiplies the wet signal, before the band filter and the resonator, by
  exp(U(Drive); 0.17783, 5.6234),
  which is −15 to +15 dB with no saturation. The default 0.5 gives +0.12 dB.
- **X.** StereoWidth w mixes the two resonator outputs:
  - left = (½ + ½w)·left resonator + (½ − ½w)·right resonator;
  - right is the same with the sides exchanged.

  It acts on the wet part only.
- **X.** The left resonator is fed by the left wet input and the right resonator by the right.
  Output = dry gain × input + width mix of the resonators, on each channel. An impulse on the
  left input alone leaves the right output at the floor (≤ 2 × 10⁻²⁰) when StereoWidth is 1, and
  the left output bit-identical to the stereo case. The output carries an added floor of about
  10⁻²² that does not depend on the input.
- **X.** Sine steady-state gains match these rules and REQ-005 to 008 within 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ dB and
  0.06° (cases DCO-016).

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-005 — modal resonance types, modes and quality

- **X.** ResonanceType 0 to 4 (Beam, Marimba, String, Membrane, Plate) are modal. For constant
  parameters, each resonator is a sum of independent two-pole resonances (modes), plus one weak
  bleed resonance (REQ-007). Mode k's nominal angular frequency is
  w_k = 2π·261.62·A(p)·r_k·A(i·log₂ r_k) rad/s. Here:
  - p is the pitch in octaves (REQ-006);
  - i is the inharmonicity (REQ-007);
  - A is the 2ˣ approximation of REQ-006;
  - r_k is the mode's ratio.
- **X.** Ratios r_k, k = 0, 1, …:
  - **Beam:** (β_k/4.730)², with β = 4.730, 7.853, 10.996, then (k + 1.5)π: 1, 2.756, 5.404, 8.933,
    13.34, ….
  - **Marimba:** (β_k/4.730)², with β = 4.730, 9.413, 15.450, 20.710, 24.580, then
    (1.4142k + 2.1213)π: 1, 3.960, 10.67, 19.17, 27.00, ….
  - **String:** k + 1.
  - **Membrane and Plate,** with R = exp(⌊U(Ratio)⌋; 1, 20) and N modes:
    - Let M = ⌊√(R·N)⌋ and Q = ⌊√(N/R)⌋; each is increased by 1 when its successor squared
      equals its argument.
    - Every pair (m, n) with 1 ≤ m ≤ M + 1 and 1 ≤ n ≤ Q + 1, listed m-major, gives a ratio.
      Membrane: √(m² + (Rn)²)/√(1 + R²). Plate: (m² + (Rn)²)/(1 + R²).
    - The pairs are sorted by ratio, stably, and the first N are kept.
- **X.** ResonatorQuality 0 to 3 (Eco, Low, Med, High) allows at most N = 4, 16, 30 or 70 modes.
  The first mode with w_k ≥ (5π/6)·fs (frequency at or above 5/12 of the sample rate) and all
  later modes are absent. For example, Beam at High has 12 modes at 44.1 kHz, the highest at
  18,033 Hz.
- **X.** For constant parameters, each channel's resonator output for input x has this transfer
  function, with z⁻¹ a one-frame delay:

  H(z) = 3000·[Σ_k c_k·E_k(h)·E_k(l)·(1 − z⁻²)/(1 + a1_k z⁻¹ + a2_k z⁻²) + bleed term]

  The terms, with fs the sample rate:
  - θ_k = w_k/fs;
  - α_k = (π/(π − θ_k))·sin θ_k·d_k/w_k, with d_k from REQ-007;
  - a1_k = −2 cos θ_k/(1 + α_k);
  - a2_k = (1 − α_k)/(1 + α_k);
  - c_k = α_k·1.01097·t_k/(2d_k(1 + α_k)), with the brightness tilt t_k from REQ-007;
  - E_k(h) and E_k(l) are the mode's weights at the strike point h and the pickup point l
    (REQ-008).

  The frequency and decay of each mode are those of the poles of its denominator. A mode with
  E_k(h)·E_k(l) = 0 is absent.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-006 — pitch

- **X.** Frequency v sets the pitch p = lin(U(v); −4, 4) octaves relative to 261.62 Hz.
  Frequency 0.5 gives 261.62 Hz (render 261.624 Hz, String).
- **X.** Detune d = lin(B(Detune); −1/12, 1/12) octave raises the left resonator by d and lowers
  the right by d. Detune 0.5 gives 269.346 Hz left and 254.176 Hz right.
- **X.** Octaves become frequency ratios by
  A(x) = 2^⌊x⌋·(1 + t + t²·(0.5 + 0.200064t)), with t = (x − ⌊x⌋)·ln 2. A is exact at whole
  octaves and up to about 1 cent sharp between them. Frequency 0.5625 gives 377.341 Hz
  (exact 2ᵖ would give 377.122 Hz).
- **X.** The pitch is limited to −5 to +67/12 octaves, LFO included.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-007 — decay, material, brightness, inharmonicity and bleed

- **X.** Decay T = exp(⌊U(Decay)⌋; 0.05, 35) s. FreqDamping (material) m = lin(⌊B(v)⌋; −1, 1).
  With L_k = log₂ r_k:
  - e_k = (5 − L_k)·min(m, 1) for m ≥ 0;
  - e_k = −max(m, −1)·L_k for m < 0;
  - d_k = 8·A(e_k)/T.
- **X.** Inharmonics i = lin(⌊B(v)⌋; −1, 1), and it enters as i³ limited to −1..1.
- **X.** AmpFreq (brightness) b = lin(⌊B(v)⌋; −1, 1) gives the tilt t_k = A((L_k − 2)·b).
- **X.** Bleed adds a resonance at the last mode's angle θ_K, but only when no mode was dropped
  under REQ-005:
  - its damping is α_H = 32·(π/(π − θ_K))·sin θ_K·d_K/w_K;
  - its numerator is b_H·g·(1 − z⁻¹)², with b_H = ((1 + cos θ_K)/2)·1.01097·t_K/((1 + α_H)·w_K)
    and g = exp(⌊U(Bleed)⌋; 0.01, 1), so its minimum is 0.01, not 0;
  - its denominator has the form of REQ-005, with α_H.
- **X.** Measured at 44.1 kHz, String, FreqDamping 0: the 261.6 Hz mode falls by 60 dB in
  0.2223 s at Decay 0.25, 1.1585 s at 0.5 and 5.736 s at 0.75. Higher modes fall slightly faster.
  FreqDamping −1 shortens the higher modes (the second mode 0.5727 s at Decay 0.5). FreqDamping
  +1 shortens the lower ones.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-008 — strike and pickup positions

- **X.** The strike point is h = lin(⌊P(ExcitationX)⌋; 0.05, 0.95), limited to 0.02..0.98. The
  left resonator's pickup is l = lin(⌊P(ListeningXL)⌋; 0.01, 0.99). The right resonator's is the
  same with ListeningXR. Each channel has one pickup.
- **X.** For Beam, Marimba and String, mode k's weight at a point u is a linear interpolation
  on a coarse grid:
  - G = N + 2 points;
  - T_k(j) = sin(π(k + 1)j/(N + 1)) for j = 0 … N + 1;
  - q = u·(G − 1), j = min(⌊q⌋, G − 2), f = q − j;
  - E_k(u) = ½·(T_k(j) + f·(T_k(j + 1) − T_k(j))).
- **X.** For Membrane and Plate the weight of mode (m, n) is a bilinear interpolation:
  - G = ⌊√N⌋ + 3;
  - the grid values are sin(πmi/(G − 1))·sin(πnj/(G − 1));
  - the point is (u, 0.44375);
  - the result is halved.
- **X.** ExcitationX 0 strikes the centre, and the even harmonics of a String are absent (−119 dB
  or lower). Host values −1 to 1 reach strike points 0.277 to 0.723. Host values 0 to 1 reach
  0.5 to 0.723. Each channel follows only its own pickup value; the other channel is unchanged
  within 4.1 × 10⁻²¹.
- **S.** A change of a pickup value moves linearly to the new point over 4,000 frames (200 steps
  of 20 frames). This was not rendered.
- **S-cond (A1).** For stored values, ExcitationX and the pickups are the host values above.

- **X.** ResonanceType 5 (Pipe) and 6 (Tube) are waveguide resonances, without the modes of

  - Tube's even harmonics are at least 68 dB below its fundamental, and its third is −16 dB;

- **S.** ResonatorQuality, FreqDamping, Inharmonics, AmpFreq, the positions and Bleed have no
  effect on Pipe and Tube. This was not rendered.
- **X.** Fundamentals at Frequency 0.5, Decay 1:

  | Setting | 44.1 kHz | 48 kHz |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pipe, Radius 0.5, Opening 1 | 251.096 Hz | 251.271 Hz |
  | Tube, Radius 0.5 | 241.364 Hz | 241.687 Hz |
  | Pipe, Radius 1 | 258.339 Hz | — |
  | Pipe, Opening 0.3 | 234.444 Hz | — |
  | Tube, Radius 0 | 173.067 Hz | — |

  Both types lie below the nominal 261.62 Hz, by more as Radius decreases.
- **U.** A closed-form description of the Pipe and Tube waveforms, and Radius and Opening values

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-010 — band filter

- **X.** FilterOn inserts a band filter in the wet path, after Drive and before the resonator.
  It is a second-order low-pass at f·A(bw/2) followed by a second-order high-pass at f/A(bw/2):
  - both are RBJ cookbook forms with Q 0.707;
  - both corner frequencies are limited to 50..18,000 Hz;
  - f = exp(U(v₂₈); 50, 18000) Hz and bw = lin(c; 0.5, 9) octaves, where c = 14.941176v₂₉ − 7.470588
    is used directly as the controller.

  Off, the wet signal passes unchanged.
- **X.** Cases DCO-019 (defaults; 200 Hz with bandwidth 1) agree with this description within
  6 × 10⁻⁵ rel RMS and 0.004 dB per third octave.
- **S.** Coefficient changes ramp over 30 frames. Switching on or off fades over ⌊fs/100⌋ frames.
  The ramps were not rendered.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-011 — LFO

- **X.** With LfoOnOff on and LfoSync Free, the LFO adds to both resonators' pitch:
  - amount·S(φ) octaves, with amount = lin(U(LfoAmount); 0, 1);
  - S(φ) = 6.094263φ + 6.094263φ² − 85.31969φ³ + 121.88526φ⁴ − 48.754105φ⁵ for the Sine shape;
  - the phase φ advances by rate/fs per frame, from 0 at the first processed frame, with
    rate = exp(U(LfoRate); 0.01, 10) Hz;
  - in Phase mode (LfoStereoMode 0) the right channel's phase is φ + lin(Deg(LfoPhase); 0, 1),
    where Deg(v) = 127v/360 for v < 180 and 0.35v + 1 otherwise.

  The resonators read the pitch every 200 frames and hold it in between. Case DCO-020: rate
  2.539 Hz, ±0.302 octave, right channel half a cycle later, within 0.1 Hz of this rule.
- **S.** The shape list: Square (−1 then +1), Triangle, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Sample & Hold (phase
  at twice the rate) and Random Ramp. Spin mode runs the right channel at rate·(1 + spin). These
  were not rendered.
- **X, U.** Sample & Hold and Random Ramp draw from a generator that the device seeds from the
  clock each time it builds its engine: at creation and at every sample-rate change. Their
  output depends on that seed (X). Inferred: in Live it differs between instances and sessions.
  Effect on T1: these two shapes are graded only as non-silent, bounded output; no exact
  render is expected.
- **U.** LfoSync on (tempo-synced rate and phase reset at transport start). The transport values
  Live passes are unknown. Effect on T1: synced LFO settings are not verifiable.

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-012 — behavior over time

- **X.** After creation the output remains at its approximately 10⁻²² numerical floor for
  100 frames (not bitwise zero). From frame 100 the dry and wet gains
  rise linearly over 100 frames to their values (DryWet 0: 0.009743 at frame 100, 0.974309 from
  frame 199).
- **S.** A parameter value sent between host blocks takes effect at the next block. Changes then
  ramp:
  - Drive and StereoWidth over 10 ms;
  - Frequency, Detune, FineTranspose and LfoAmount over 1 ms;
  - DryWet gains toward new values over 100 frames, retargeted every 100 frames;
  - pickups over 4,000 frames;
  - the other resonator values step at the next coefficient update, which comes at most every
    200 frames.
- **X.** Changing the sample rate rebuilds the device and restores its state with six significant
  digits. The output then differs from a device created at that rate by at most 1.2 × 10⁻⁶
  (rel RMS 3.3 × 10⁻⁵). This is inside the metric.
- **X.** A device reset alone turns a Tube into a Pipe until ResonanceType is sent again. Live
  sends it again after every reset (S, REQ-001), so this is not audible.
- **S.** The device reports that it may stop processing after fs/10 frames whose magnitude is at
  most 10⁻⁵ on both channels.

## Timing and state

- **Units.** Frames at the stated sample rate. Pitch in octaves relative to 261.62 Hz.
- **Latency.** None. An input impulse at frame n gives its dry part and the first resonator
  output at frame n (X).
- **Persistent state.** None beyond the stored parameters. The device's ringing state lives only
  in a running instance.
- **Determinism.** Deterministic for a given input, parameter set and history (REQ-001, 012),
  except the random LFO shapes (REQ-011).

## Comparison metric

Proposed as a general T1 device-audio criterion of ADR 0004. The finite
use of this criterion is separately bounded by the
[handoff plan](device-corpus-handoff-plan.md#review-outcome--2026-10-19); approval
of that finite package does not approve unlisted modes or scenarios. A candidate render
of a case passes when it meets every line that applies, measured on the case's frames after
any start-up ramp.

| Signal | Comparator | Tolerance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Modal types, impulse input | Each mode with weight at least 10⁻³ of the strongest, measured in candidate and reference with the same demodulation estimator (appendix). A mode is graded only if the estimate from the reference render is within 10⁻⁴ of its REQ-005 pole frequency; closely spaced or heavily damped modes are not resolved | Frequency within 4 binary32 ulp bounds. The bound is 3·2⁻²⁵/θ² + 2⁻²³ relative, with θ = 2πf/fs. At 44.1 kHz the tolerance is 4.0 × 10⁻³ at 66 Hz and 2.6 × 10⁻⁴ at 262 Hz. Per-frame log radius ρ within 8·2⁻²⁵/\|ρ\| relative. Complex amplitude within 5 × 10⁻³ |
| Modal types, impulse input | Waveform, the 256 frames from the impulse | Rel RMS within 2 × 10⁻³ |
| Steady-state sine | Complex gain fitted over the last 8,192 frames | 0.01 dB and 0.5° |
| Noise | Third-octave band levels, 80 Hz to 16 kHz, from frame 8,192 | 0.01 dB |
| Pipe, Tube, filter, dry path | Waveform after the impulse or after frame 8,192 | Rel RMS within 10⁻⁴ |
| LFO pitch | Instantaneous fundamental, averaged over 200 frames | 0.2 Hz at 261.62 Hz |
| Timing | Start-up silence and ramps | Exact frames |

Why not a sample-by-sample maximum error. The device's coefficients are binary32. One ulp
in each denominator coefficient moves a low mode's frequency by up to 3·2⁻²⁵/θ² relative.
Over a long ring that grows into a large phase error, although the sound does not change.
The original is itself sensitive at that scale:

- one-ulp changes of the substituted libm results move a 66 Hz mode by 6.8 × 10⁻⁴ and change
  the waveform by 4 % after 0.28 s;
- the arm64 release slice has 232 fused multiply-adds that the x86_64 slice lacks.

The largest differences between the reference renders and REQ-005 to 008 are 1.0 ulp bound in
frequency, 2.04 in log radius and 2.8 × 10⁻⁴ in amplitude, against which the tolerances leave a
margin of four or more. Membrane is the exception, at 1.19, 4.4 and 2.3 × 10⁻³: its closely
spaced modes limit the estimator, and the margin there is about two. On paths that do not
resonate the effects are 10⁻⁵ or smaller, so a waveform tolerance can be used there.

## Acceptance cases

Expectations are X renders of the original x86_64 code under REQ-001's protocol. None has been
run against Live, and under ADR 0003 none will be. Kinds: P positive, B boundary, T timing,
U not graded.

# Corpus device: signal chain and resonator (decompiled)

**Question.** What does Live 12.4.3's bundled Corpus audio effect compute, from
Live's parameter call down to each output sample? This was read from the
decompiled bundle only. Nothing was executed, and no output was compared with
Corpus's real sound.

**Answer.**
- **Engine.** Corpus is a small modular engine of linked per-channel modules
  (*Inferred:* Applied Acoustics–style, from the module and class names).
- **Signal path.** The input splits into dry and wet through a panpot. The wet
  part goes through a clean gain (Live's Drive) and a band filter into one
  `ab_resonator` per channel. The resonator outputs pass a width crossfade, and
  the dry signal is added back.
- **Resonator models.** Five body types are banks of two-pole modal filters
  with fixed mode-ratio tables. Pipe and Tube are two-line waveguides.
- **Pitch.** Pitch arrives in octaves around 261.62 Hz from a pitch hub, which
  adds the LFO and Detune.
- **Parameters.** Live sends 38 numbered parameters, and the device uses the
  first 37. Resonator values are
  quantized to 128 controller steps.

Live's side is traced in the [device parameter mapping](device-parameter-mapping-native.md)
(N5). It confirms the Live names for host indices 0–36 below. Live passes each
stored Corpus value unchanged, except FilterMidFreq, which it maps from Hz to
0–1 on a log10 scale over 50–18,000.

## Host parameters

`_SetParameterA` calls the wrapper at `0xd75c`. That function converts the host
value *v* to a controller value *c* in 0–127 and sends it to a module. The
constructor at `0xc40c` builds the 37-entry routing table. The module drivers
map *c* to a value:

| Driver | Mapping |
| --- | --- |
| Linear | *c* = 64 gives the midpoint, otherwise *c*/127 |
| Exponential | min·(max/min)^(*c*/127) |
| Cubic | (*c*/127)³, with 0.125 at *c* = 64 |
| Integer | Controller 64 gives 63 |

The resonator's handler (`0x20fc8`) truncates every value to an integer
controller.

The conversions in the table:
- **D:** `v ≤ 0.5 ? 128v : 126v+1`
- **B:** `v < 0 ? 63.5v+63.5 : 63v+64`

## Module graph

Built in `0x5ca8`; each per-channel module exists twice, and the left instance
forwards every parameter message to the right.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    IN[Stereo input] --> PAN[DryWet panpot]
    PAN -->|wet| G[Gain] --> F[Band filter] --> R[ab_resonator x2]
    LFO[Stereo LFO] --> HUB[Pitch hub] -->|pitch, gate| R
    R --> W[Width crossfade] --> MIX[plus]
    PAN -->|dry| MIX --> OUT[Stereo output]
```

The engine processes sub-blocks of up to 512 samples and applies parameter
messages once per host block. The net output gain is unity.

## Resonator

**Types** (builders at `0x243e8`, `0x24ee4`, `0x25210` and `0x257b4`). Each
entry gives the ratios r_k:

| Live index | Internal | Model | Ratios r_k |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 Beam | modal | (β_k/4.730)²; β = 4.730, 7.853, 10.996, then (k+1.5)π |
| 1 | 2 Marimba | modal | β = 4.730, 9.413, 15.450, 20.710, 24.580, then (1.4142k+2.1213)π |
| 2 | 3 String | modal | k+1 |
| 3 | 4 Membrane | modal, 2-D | √(m²+(Rn)²)/√(1+R²), with R = Ratio |
| 4 | 5 Plate | modal, 2-D | (m²+(Rn)²)/(1+R²) |
| 5 | 7 Pipe | waveguide | — |
| 6 | 6 Tube | waveguide | — |

This confirms the label order that the Corpus demo had to assume. The Marimba
ratios start 1, 3.96, 10.67; Membrane at R = 1.5 starts 1, 1.387, 1.754.

**Modal model** (`0x1f3f8`):
- **Mode count.** Quality selects 4, 16, 30 or 70 modes. There is no
  oversampling.
- **Mode frequency.** Mode k's angular frequency is
  1643.807·2^p·r_k·r_k^(inh³), with pitch p in octaves.
- **Dropped modes.** A mode at or above 5/12 of the sample rate ends the list
  and turns Bleed off.
- **Damping.** Each mode is a two-pole resonator. Its damping is
  8·2^e / decay, where *e* tilts the damping by `tone` across the modes'
  log-ratios. Gain is tilted by `amp_freq`.
- **Hit and pickups.** Excitation and pickup weights come from a coarse
  mode-shape table with linear (1-D) or bilinear (2-D) interpolation, not from
  analytic sines. Each channel is mono: the left resonator listens at
  ListeningXL and the right at ListeningXR.
- **Update rate.** Coefficients update at most every 200 samples. Pickups move
  linearly over 4,000 samples.
- **Bleed.** A two-pole high-pass of the excitation is added before the ×3000
  output scale.

**Waveguide** (`0x23670`):
- **Lines.** Two 2,048-sample delay lines, each about fs/(2^p·523.24) − 0.75
  samples (half that for Tube). Reads use 5-tap Lagrange interpolation.
- **Feedback.** −0.999, with a 30 Hz DC blocker on the input.
- **Reflection.** A first-order reflection filter set by Radius and, for Pipe,
  Opening. Tube's loop is inverted once more.
- **Loss.** Per-trip loss is exp(−4/(decay·261.62·2^p)).

## The other modules

- **Panpot (DryWet).** The wet gain is P(a/4) and the dry gain P(0.25 − a/4),
  with P(t) = 6√3·t(1−t)(1−2t). Gains ramp over 100 samples.
- **Gain (Drive).** A linear gain of −15 to +15 dB with a 10 ms ramp. There is
  no saturation.
- **Band filter.** An RBJ low-pass at f·2^(bw/2) feeds an RBJ high-pass at
  f/2^(bw/2), both Q 0.707. Coefficients ramp over 30 samples, and on/off fades
  over 10 ms.
- **Width.** L' = (½+½w)L + (½−½w)R, applied to the resonated signal only.
- **LFO.** Seven shapes, in order: Sine (polynomial), Square, Triangle, Ramp
  Up, Ramp Down, Sample and Hold (phase at double rate), Random Ramp.
  - Free rate: 0.01·1000^(c/127) Hz. Sync uses a 22-entry bar table from 8 to
    1/64.
  - Stereo: Phase mode applies a fixed offset to the right channel; Spin mode
    runs the right channel faster.
  - Output adds to pitch: Amount 1 is ±1 octave.
- **Pitch hub.**
  - With MidiPitch off, pitch is the fixed pitch (from Frequency) plus the LFO,
    with Detune added on the left and subtracted on the right.
  - With MidiPitch on, pitch is (note − 60)/12 plus bend, Fine and Transpose,
    with the highest held note winning.
  - The gate is open unless MidiGate is on and no note is held.

## Quirks a faithful port reproduces

1. Resonator parameters move in 128 steps.
2. The integer driver maps controller 64 to 63: Transpose +16 sounds as +15.
3. Pitch and LFO changes reach the modal filters at most every 200 samples.
4. Pipe and Tube ring below their nominal pitch because the reflection filter
   adds delay. At 48 kHz with default Radius and Opening, the port gives
   251.0 Hz and 241.2 Hz against a nominal 261.62 Hz.
5. Bleed's minimum is 0.01, not 0.
6. Bleed turns off when any mode passes 5/12 of the sample rate.

# Device audio by extracted execution (T1.2 feasibility gate)

**Question.** Workstream T1.2 of [roadmap revision 3](native-decompilation-roadmap.md#revision-3--t1-completion-plan-2026-10-18)
starts with a gate. Can a harness load a device bundle's x86_64 slice, drive it the way Live does
and render audio? Are the renders deterministic and bit-for-bit repeatable? Can they be explained
by the static [Corpus DSP model](corpus-dsp-static.md)? Can the instrument path (note events in,
audio out) be driven? What metric should a device spec state, and what would the other five
devices need?

**Answer (X, draft). The gate passes.**

- **Loading.** A loader adapted from the [extracted-execution harness](extracted-execution.md)
  loads the Corpus, Analog, Tension, Collision and Electric slices. It creates instances and
  renders through the bundles' own `CalcA`. No exception path, fault or unbound import was hit.
- **Repeatability.** Corpus renders are bit-identical in these cases:
  - re-runs in new processes (6 of 6);
  - host blocks of 64, 256, 333 and 2,048 frames against 512, with constant parameters;
  - flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero against the default MXCSR;
  - another clock value for the random seed, except where a random LFO shape is selected.
- **Static model.** Against the [static model](corpus-dsp-static.md) of the modal resonator:
  - mode frequencies agree within about one binary32 ulp of the mode's filter coefficients
    (41 impulse cases, both channels);
  - decay rates agree within about two ulps;
  - mode amplitudes, and with them the strike and pickup position effects, agree to 2.8 × 10⁻⁴
    (Membrane, with closely spaced modes, 2.3 × 10⁻³);
  - steady-state sine gains agree to 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ dB, and noise third-octave levels to 0.004 dB.
- **Port.** Every difference from the [traced port](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/demos/corpus-traced/index.html)
  is explained ([differences](#differences-and-their-explanations)).
- **Instrument path.** Analog plays notes from 16-byte events. Its note-on and note-off take effect
  on a 1 ms control grid, by an exact rule that holds for all 300 tested events.
- **Other devices.** Tension and Electric render notes after six more bindings. Collision runs, but
  its parameter path is not understood yet. Amp and Cabinet stop in a static initializer at
  `dladdr` and need a much larger macOS emulation ([effort](#effort-for-the-other-five-devices)).

## How Live drives a bundle

Live side (S, from [N5](device-parameter-mapping-native.md#how-live-loads-a-bundle)). Live
loads `<resources>/Devices/Mac/<Name>.bundle` and resolves the seven exports by name. It queries
`GetPlugInfoU`. It calls `CreateInstanceU()` and then `SetSampleRateU(handle, rate)` with the
current rate. Parameters are flushed as `SetParameterA(handle, index, value)` with the index
order and conversions of N5 and [N6](device-tables-native.md). The reviewed
[processing-protocol trace](device-host-protocol.md#initialization-reset-sample-rate-and-teardown)
distinguishes ordinary Reset/NewRate (no warm-up) from ResetAndDispatch: four
1,024-frame helper requests, then reset and cached index-0 restoration for the
reset-capable primary. This corrects the earlier one-warm-up shorthand; the
exact initialization/reset audio remains unknown. Live sets flush-to-zero around `SetSampleRateU`,
`SetParameterA` and `ResetA` (arm64).

Bundle side (X and S, x86_64 disassembly in this packet). The calling convention is System V.

| Export | Corpus x86_64 | Analog x86_64 | Arguments and result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateInstanceU` | `0x23b0` | `0x1fd70` | () → instance |
| `DestroyInstanceU` | `0x2460` | `0x1fdf0` | (instance) |
| `SetSampleRateU` | `0x2490` | `0x1fe60` | (instance, rate in Hz as a 64-bit integer) → 1 |
| `GetPlugInfoU` | `0x2930` | `0x1fed0` | (selector, out, size) → 1 if answered |
| `CalcA` | `0x29c0` | `0x1ff80` | (instance, frames, L, R, event count, events, transport, flag); the last two are stack arguments |
| `SetParameterA` | `0x2d60` | `0x20290` | (instance, index as int, value as float in `xmm0`) |
| `ResetA` | `0x2d80` | `0x20310` | (instance) |

The `CalcA` arguments that H4 and N5 left unknown, as the bundles read them:

- **Buffers.** `L` and `R` are processed in place: input in, output out.
- **Events.** 16 bytes each: a 64-bit frame offset, then status, data 1 and data 2 bytes. Corpus
  queues an event with frame − 1 when the frame is non-zero; Analog uses the frame as given.
- **Transport.** {int32 playing, padding, binary64 position, binary64 tempo}. Analog reads it
  unconditionally. Corpus accepts a null pointer.
- **Flag.** For Corpus, a non-zero `*flag` on entry means input is present; otherwise the engine
  reads silence. On return, Corpus clears it after fs/10 quiet frames (S). Analog writes 1 while
  it still sounds (X: 1 during the note, 0 after the release).
- **Block size.** `GetPlugInfoU` selector 5 answers 512 for both bundles. Corpus also processes
  internally in sub-blocks of at most 512 frames (S).

The selector answers measured (X) equal H4's static table.

**Not known (U).** Which frame base Live uses for events (0- or 1-based); what Live passes as the
transport and the input flag; Live's real block sizes; and when it runs the reset sequence.
The harness passes transport {0, 0.0, 120.0} and input flag 1 for effects (0 for instruments).

## Harness

[`harness/`](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/r2/t12-device-dsp-v1/harness/xdev.c) is a copy
of `tools/xexec` adapted to bundles. `tools/xexec` itself is unchanged. The copy is built to
`/var/tmp/sound-analysis/t12-xdev/xdev`. Changes:

- **Mapping.** The x86_64 slice is picked from the universal file and mapped at a fixed slide,
  `0x200000000`, because the image base 0 cannot be mapped. Rebases apply the slide.
  Zero-fill sections are cleared.
- **Imports.** Every unbound import gets its own slot in a `PROT_NONE` region. A call or a data
  read through it stops the run with `TRAP <symbol>`. The `__mod_init_func` initializers run
  after binding, as dyld would run them. Exports are found in the symbol table.
- **Driver.** A C script interpreter calls the exports directly, with real stack arguments for
  `CalcA`, and writes binary32 output. There is no limit of 256 calls.
- **Bindings.** Each binding keeps the contract its call sites rely on. `results/*.json` lists
  the imports each run used.

| Group | Binding |
| --- | --- |
| libc, memory, strings | glibc |
| libm | glibc 2.39. Bundles call `sinf`, `cosf`, `expf`, `logf`, `tanf`, `atanf`, `cbrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `modff`, `ldexpf`, `floorf` and others; Tension and Electric also `__exp10`, `pow`, `log10f`, `fmodf` |
| macOS-only | `__sincosf_stret`, `__sincos_stret` (results packed as the ABI returns them), `memset_pattern16`, `newlocale` (C locale only; macOS mask values ignored), `__stderrp`, `_DefaultRuneLocale` (a C-locale table with Apple's `_CTYPE` bits, runetype at offset 60), `__maskrune` (no classes above 127) |
| `rand`, `srand` | The FreeBSD-lineage Park–Miller generator (16807, modulus 2³¹ − 1). This is inferred from Apple's libc lineage, not read from Apple's binary |
| `time` | Fixed at 0, or at `XDEV_TIME`. Both bundles seed `rand` with `srand(time(0))` while building their engines (Corpus `0x199c0`) |
| C++ ABI | `__dynamic_cast` and the three `__cxxabiv1` type_info vtables from libstdc++, which implements the same Itanium ABI. Exceptions, `__cxa_throw` and unwinding are trapped |
| libc++ (`std::__1`) | 59 members reimplemented in `xdev_cxx.c` on libc++'s x86_64 layouts: `std::string` standard layout (checked in the bundles' inline code), `ios_base`, `basic_ios`, `basic_streambuf` slots, `istream` (`get`, `unget`, `putback`, `tellg`, `seekg`, `>>` int and unsigned), `ostream` (`<<` int, unsigned long, bool, float, double; `put`, `flush`), the sentries, `locale` and `ctype<char>` |

The bundles need the stream shim. Corpus builds its module graph from text written to
`ostringstream`s and parsed with `sscanf`. It constructs its engine state from an embedded text
patch read through an `istringstream`. On every sample-rate change it saves that state through a
`stringstream` and reads it back. Floats are written with libc++'s default `%.*g`, precision 6,
and read back with `atof`. A traced rate change (`XDEV_TRACE_OSTREAM`) wrote 51 floats, all at
precision 6. No stream extraction set the fail bit (`cxx-failbits 0` in every log).

### Differences and their explanations

1. **Start-up.** The port ramps the panpot gains from frame 0. The original is silent for the
   first 100 frames and then ramps over the next 100. This explains the port's 4–11 % error on
   inputs that start at frame 0. The report's "both gains start at 0" is right, but it leaves out
   that the first ramp starts only after 100 frames.
2. **Precision.** The port computes the coefficients in binary64. The original computes and
   stores them in binary32. Low modes are the most sensitive, and their phase drifts: rel RMS
   4 × 10⁻² at 66 Hz. The static model with binary32 rounding is within one ulp bound.
3. **Pipe and Tube pitch.** [Corpus DSP](corpus-dsp-static.md#quirks-a-faithful-port-reproduces)
   quirk 4 and CD-C07 give 251.0 Hz and 241.2 Hz at 48 kHz. X and the port both give 251.271
   and 241.687 Hz; the page's figures were rough readings. The drops are 3.96 % and 7.62 %, as
   CD-C07 says ("about 4 % and 8 %").

   ([determinism](#determinism)).
5. **DecayOnNoteOff.** The port passes the stored value through the D rule. Live sends 1 − v
   (N5). It matters only while MidiGate closes the gate, which no case exercised.
6. **Random LFO shapes.** These are seeded from the clock in the original and from `Math.random`
   in the port. Neither can be compared sample by sample.

No difference between X and the static model remains unexplained.

  48 at 48 kHz), counted from the first processed frame. An event at frame f takes effect at the
  start g of the grid period containing f. If g lies in an earlier host block, it takes effect at
  g plus one period instead. The first changed output frame is the one after that point. A
  note-on can therefore sound up to a period minus one frame before its timestamp. The rule held
  for all 250 note-ons (blocks of 512, 64 and 333; both rates) and all 50 note-offs tested
  (`timing`).

  remaining gaps are canonical there; the feasibility run above is historical.

## Floating-point substitutions and the arm64 slice

**libm.** [`libm_sensitivity.py`](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/r2/t12-device-dsp-v1/libm_sensitivity.py)
re-renders 10 cases with every inexact libm result moved one ulp up, and again one ulp down. It
leaves out floor, modf, ldexp, fabs and sqrt, which are exact everywhere (`results/libm_sensitivity.json`).

| Case | Rel RMS, first 256 samples | Rel RMS, whole window | Largest mode-frequency shift |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Corpus defaults, String High, Membrane High | 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ to 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ | 2.6 × 10⁻³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ | 4.3 × 10⁻⁵ |
| Corpus 66 Hz String | 9.8 × 10⁻⁴ | 4.0 × 10⁻² | 6.8 × 10⁻⁴ |
| Corpus Tube, 48 kHz | 6.4 × 10⁻⁷ | 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ | — |
| Corpus noise, sine 1 kHz | 2 × 10⁻⁶ to 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ | 2 × 10⁻⁶ to 9.5 × 10⁻⁵ | — |
| Analog C4 | — | 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.9 × 10⁻³ | f0 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ |

Inferred: if Apple's libm is within one ulp of glibc, the substitution moves Corpus mode
frequencies by about one ulp bound. It does not move them beyond that.

**arm64.** [`fma_scan.py`](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/r2/t12-device-dsp-v1/fma_scan.py)
decodes the arm64 `__text` (`results/fma_scan.txt`):

- Corpus has 232 fused multiply-adds in 54 functions: 67 in the modal resonator `0x1f3f8`, 36 in
  the waveguide `0x23670`, 7 in the panpot `0x1dfec` and 6 in the parameter wrapper `0xd75c`.
- Analog has 814 in 130 functions.
- The x86_64 slices have none.

Inferred: arm64 renders differ from x86_64 renders by rounding at the same scale as the libm
effect. That is about one ulp bound in each mode frequency, plus per-sample rounding in the
filters. It was not measured: no arm64 execution is authorised.

**Consequence for the metric.** A maximum absolute error over a long resonant render is not
usable. A one-ulp change moves a 66 Hz mode by 6.8 × 10⁻⁴, which is 4 % of the waveform after
0.28 s. Per-device metrics must therefore be stated as follows.

- **Corpus modal types**, on the modes the estimator resolves in the reference render:
  - per-mode frequency within 4 ulp bounds;
  - decay rate within 8 ulp bounds of a2;
  - complex amplitude within 5 × 10⁻³.

  Elsewhere the largest render-to-model differences are 1.0 ulp bound, 2.04 ulp bounds and
  2.8 × 10⁻⁴, a margin of four or more. On Membrane they are 1.19, 4.4 and 2.3 × 10⁻³, a margin
  of only about two, because its closely spaced modes limit the estimator. For all Corpus modal
  types:
  - waveform rel RMS within 2 × 10⁻³ over the first 256 samples after an impulse;
  - third-octave noise levels within 0.01 dB;
  - sine steady-state within 0.01 dB and 0.5°.
- **Pipe, Tube and the non-resonant paths.** These are insensitive (10⁻⁵), so a waveform rel RMS
  of 10⁻⁴ over the whole render can be used.
- **Analog.** Event timing exact, and f0 within 10⁻⁵. Its spectral metric is to be calibrated in
  its own spec.

## Limits

- **What X shows.** X shows what the x86_64 bundle code computes for the stated calls, inputs and
  substitutions. It does not show that Live makes the same calls. The call sequence is N5's
  static reading, with the unknowns listed [above](#how-live-drives-a-bundle).
- **Substitutions.** These are libm, `rand` (inferred Park–Miller), `time`, the C locale and the
  libc++ shim. The shim follows libc++ semantics for well-formed text. Overflow and other error
  paths of stream extraction were never reached, and they are implemented only to libc++'s
  documented behavior.
- **The arm64 slice was not executed.** Its fused operations are counted only.
- **Coverage.** Corpus's MIDI side-chain (MidiPitch, MidiGate, Transpose, FineTranspose,
  PitchBendRange, DecayOnNoteOff, MidiMode), LFO Sync and Spin, filter settings other than the two
  rendered, and parameter changes during a render were not run.
- **Retention.** The renders in `raw/` are retained. Re-runs, variants, sweeps, perturbed and port
  renders are written to `/var/tmp/sound-analysis/t12-xdev/`. Their SHA-256 and comparisons are
  in `results/`.

# ADR 0003: No reference execution; the project finishes on the Linux workstation

## Decision and authority

Adopted by user direction on 2026-10-18: "mac observation not possible; we are
finishing the proj on this x86 machine". No macOS host is available. Neither
Mach-O slice of the reference build can run on the Linux x86_64 workstation, and
no compatibility layer is authorized. All remaining analysis, specification,
handoff, implementation and validation work happens on this workstation.

This decision narrows [ADR 0002](adr-0002-static-first-analysis.md). Static
evidence becomes the only source of reference behavior. That evidence is the
decompiled arm64 and x86_64 corpora, shipped resources, schemas, scripts and
saved documents, and published documentation.

## Extracted execution of original code

Amended by user direction on 2026-10-18: "integration test style observation is
still possible if you can compile portions of the original program on this
machine". The whole application cannot run here, but some of its own machine code can.

- **What is permitted.** The x86_64 slice can be loaded into a harness process on this
  host, and self-contained functions can be called with recorded inputs. macOS
  x86_64 and Linux x86_64 share the System V AMD64 calling convention. Execution of
  the shipped bytes counts as reference evidence of a new kind, labelled X
  (extracted execution).
- **What it shows.** It shows what the original code computes for the given
  inputs. It does not show how the application reaches that code, what state
  it holds there, or what the user sees. The harness supplies the setup, and
  every stub or replaced import is recorded with the result.
- **Slice.** Results bind to the x86_64 slice. The release target is the arm64
  slice, so arm64 equivalence is an inference. It must be checked by comparing the
  two slices' code statically, and noted wherever floating-point evaluation could
  differ (for example, fused multiply-add on arm64).
- **Recompiled decompiler output** is a static derivation, not X evidence,
  unless it is checked against X runs of the same function.
- **Tooling.** Only tools already installed are used (gcc, gdb, objdump). Adding an
  emulator for the arm64 slice needs separate user approval.

## Consequences

- **Runtime escalation.** ADR 0002's escalation rule has no whole-application
  path. A question that would have needed observation is answered by
  extracted execution where the behavior lives in a self-contained function.
  Otherwise it is answered statically or stays unknown. Unknown behavior is excluded from releases, never guessed.
- **Phase 4 probes.** The [probe batch](../research/phase4-probe-batch.md) will
  not run as planned. It is kept as the record of what observation would have
  settled. Each probe's question becomes an extracted-execution target, a
  static investigation target or a permanent unknown.
- **Specs.** A clause or case that waits on a probe stays unknown or ungraded
  and cites this decision. A static derivation stays labelled static. Neither
  is ever relabelled as observed.
- **Releases.** Released payloads are not rewritten. Their "comparison not-run"
  obligations are now permanent: no original-versus-candidate comparison will
  happen. Extracted-execution results may support a later release revision.
- **Verification.** Candidate checks compare against released expectations, which are
  static-derived or, where available, from extracted execution. Reports must say so and must not claim compatibility with
  Live. Where coverage would show a reference comparison, it records it as
  unavailable.
- **Implementation.** The candidate is built and tested on this Linux x86_64
  workstation. Clean-room separation still applies (ADR 0001, AGENTS.md).
  Implementation needs a separately restricted workspace with only released
  handoffs and neutral governance. This decision does not provision one.
